en.greeting: Hi! Today is about writing that moves people to act: rhetorical devices, the three appeals and a clear persuasive structure, used honestly. Let's start with rhythm.

steps.title: From argument to persuasion
steps.text: Quick recap, then the new part.
steps.body:
From C1 you can build an argument with evidence, rebut and concede, and use inversion for emphasis. Persuasive writing (an **op-ed**, a **petition**, an **NGO campaign letter**, a **CEO's letter to shareholders**) uses all of that to make one reader **agree and act**.
First tool: the rhythm devices.
**Tricolon** (the rule of three): three parallel parts.
**Anaphora**: the same words opening several sentences.
**Parallelism**: every item in the same grammatical form (*to protect, to cool and to connect*, not *to protect, cooling and connection*).
**Climax**: weakest → strongest, the strongest last.
If these remind you of *majas* (anafora, klimaks), you're right: similar ideas.

pairs.en: a tricolon / the rule of three

pairs.id: anafora (kata yang sama di awal kalimat)
klimaks (dari yang lemah ke yang kuat)

steps.title: Rhythm in a petition
steps.text: Lines from a practice petition to Bandung city council about Taman Melati, a fictional park.
steps.body: Notice the climax in the fourth line: money, then time, then children's health. And one C1 inversion, used once, at a key moment.

examples.en: The park gives us shade, fresh air and a place to meet.
examples.id: Taman itu memberi kita keteduhan, udara segar dan tempat untuk berkumpul. (tricolon)

examples.en: This park is where our children play. This park is where our parents walk. This park is where our neighbourhood meets.
examples.id: Taman ini tempat anak-anak kita bermain. Taman ini tempat orang tua kita berjalan-jalan. Taman ini tempat warga kita berkumpul. (anafora)

examples.en: We ask the council to stop the plan, to review the flood data and to meet the residents.
examples.id: Kami meminta dewan kota menghentikan rencana itu, meninjau data banjir dan menemui warga. (struktur sejajar)

examples.en: Paving it will cost us money, it will cost us time, and it will cost our children their health.
examples.id: Mengaspalnya akan menghabiskan uang kita, menghabiskan waktu kita, dan merenggut kesehatan anak-anak kita. (klimaks)

examples.en: Rarely has a single decision affected so many families.
examples.id: Jarang sekali satu keputusan berdampak pada begitu banyak keluarga. (inversi)

steps.title: Contrast and questions
steps.text: Next: devices that work through contrast, and the rhetorical question.
steps.body:
**Antithesis**: two opposite ideas in a balanced pair: *not X but Y* / *not X; Y*. *We are not asking for charity; we are asking for a fair chance.* The reader remembers Y.
⚠ *Not only X but also Y* **adds** Y and keeps X, so it's not antithesis: *bukan … melainkan* ≠ *tidak hanya … tetapi juga*.
**Chiasmus**: words come back in reverse order, A-B then B-A: *Good parks make good neighbours, and good neighbours make good parks.*
**Rhetorical question**: the answer is obvious, so the reader answers it silently: *Do we really want our children's only playground to be a car park?* One draws the reader in; a string of them sounds as if you have no evidence.

pairs.en: not only X but also Y
pairs.id: tidak hanya X tetapi juga Y (menambah)

steps.title: Name the device
steps.text: An op-ed in a Surabaya newspaper criticises a delayed bus project.

question.prompt: Which of these devices does the writer use? 'We were promised cleaner buses. We were promised shorter journeys. We were promised a city that works.'
options: antithesis
chiasmus
anaphora
question.explanation: **We were promised** opens all three sentences: that's **anaphora**. (It's also a tricolon, building to the biggest promise last.) There are no opposite ideas, so it isn't antithesis, and nothing comes back in reverse order, so it isn't chiasmus.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani, CEO of a textile company in Bandung, is writing to shareholders after building an expensive new factory.

question.prompt: She wants a sharp contrast. Which sentence uses antithesis correctly?
options: Our new factory is not only a cost but also an investment.
Our new factory is not a cost; it is an investment in the next twenty years.
Our new factory is not a cost; it is not cheap either.
question.explanation: **Not a cost; an investment** sets two opposite ideas against each other, and the reader remembers the second. *Not only … but also* adds the investment and keeps the cost, so it admits the factory is a burden. The third sentence has no opposite ideas at all.

steps.title: Building a persuasive case
steps.text: Devices decorate; structure persuades. Here's the plan behind a strong text.
steps.body:
**Know your reader** (a council cares about budget and voters; shareholders about profit and risk) and **frame the problem** in their terms.
Use the **three appeals**: **ethos** (why trust you), **pathos** (what they should feel), **logos** (numbers, cause and effect). Be concrete: *212 trees*, not *many trees*.
Put your **strongest argument first or last**, never buried in the middle.
Answer objections before the reader does (**prolepsis**): *Some will say a park is a luxury. In fact, …*
End with a **call to action**: who, what, by when.
Indonesian habit: a long ceremonial opening (*Dengan hormat, sehubungan dengan …*). Put the problem and the ask in the first few sentences.

steps.title: Write for your reader
steps.text: Rina is writing to the Bandung city council's budget committee about Taman Melati. Its members care most about costs.

question.prompt: Which opening is most persuasive for this reader?
options: Keeping Taman Melati costs the city about Rp 400 million a year; replacing the flood protection it gives us would cost an estimated Rp 6 billion.
Taman Melati is the heart of our neighbourhood, and every resident loves it dearly.
If the council destroys our park, Bandung will drown in floods and our children will suffer forever.
question.explanation: The first opening **frames the problem in the committee's terms** (money) with concrete numbers: logos for a reader who thinks in budgets. The second is sincere pathos, but it doesn't speak to their concern. The third is fear-mongering: an exaggerated threat that costs the writer credibility.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina wants to answer the committee's biggest worry before they raise it.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Sebagian orang akan bilang kota ini tidak mampu membiayainya.
question.solution: Some will say the city cannot afford it.
question.explanation: **Some will say …** names the objection fairly (prolepsis). Rina then answers it with evidence: *In fact, a single flood would cost far more.* Raising the objection yourself shows confidence and builds trust.

steps.title: Persuade, don't manipulate
steps.text: Last part: where persuasion ends and manipulation begins.
steps.body:
Persuasion gives good reasons; **manipulation** uses tricks that fail under a careful look, and a reader who spots one stops trusting the rest.
**Fear-mongering**: exaggerating a threat. *If the park goes, Bandung will drown.*
**False dilemma**: only two options when more exist. *Either we sell the land, or the city goes bankrupt.*
**Loaded question**: a question that hides an unproven claim. *Why is the mayor hiding the real cost?*
Emotion itself is fine: a true story is fair pathos. It's manipulation when it's exaggerated, invented or used instead of evidence.

steps.title: Spot the trick
steps.text: Here are lines from leaflets for and against a new mall in Bandung.

question.prompt: Which sentence is a false dilemma?
options: Some residents worry about traffic, and the developer has not yet published a traffic study.
Please come to the public hearing at the city hall on 20 May and give your view.
Either we build the mall, or Bandung's young people will have no future.
question.explanation: It offers only two options, when there are many other ways to create jobs for young people (other projects, training, small businesses): a **false dilemma**. The first sentence is a fair, checkable point; the second is a clear call to action.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page, for your next op-ed, petition or campaign letter.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Rhetoric and persuasion
artifact.intro: One strong device at a key moment, three appeals working together, a clear ask, and no tricks.
rows: We need shade. We need clean air. We need …
to protect, to cool and to connect
Never has this city needed a park more.
not a cost, but an investment (not: not only … but also)
Invest in your people, and your people will invest in you.
Who wants to breathe exhaust fumes on the way to school?
my 20 years / a child's story / Rp 6 billion
first or last, never in the middle
Please vote no at the meeting on 12 March.
tips: Keep lists parallel: green, quiet and shady (not green, quiet and it has trees).
Know the reader, frame the problem in their terms, and use concrete numbers.
Emotion is fair when it's true and backed by evidence; tricks destroy trust.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini tentang tulisan yang menggerakkan orang untuk bertindak: gaya bahasa retoris, tiga daya bujuk dan struktur persuasif yang jelas, dipakai dengan jujur. Kita mulai dari irama.

steps.title: Dari argumen ke persuasi
steps.text: Kilas balik singkat, lalu bagian barunya.
steps.body:
Dari C1 kamu sudah bisa membangun argumen dengan bukti, membantah dan mengakui poin lawan, dan memakai inversi untuk penekanan. Tulisan persuasif (**op-ed** atau artikel opini, **petisi**, **surat kampanye LSM**, **surat CEO kepada pemegang saham**) memakai semua itu untuk membuat satu pembaca **setuju dan bertindak**.
Alat pertama: gaya bahasa irama.
**Tricolon** (aturan tiga): tiga bagian yang sejajar.
**Anaphora**: kata yang sama membuka beberapa kalimat.
**Parallelism**: setiap bagian punya bentuk tata bahasa yang sama (*to protect, to cool and to connect*, bukan *to protect, cooling and connection*).
**Climax**: dari yang paling lemah ke yang paling kuat, yang terkuat di akhir.
Kalau ini mengingatkanmu pada *majas* (anafora, klimaks), kamu benar: idenya mirip.

pairs.en: a tricolon / the rule of three

pairs.id: anafora (kata yang sama di awal kalimat)
klimaks (dari yang lemah ke yang kuat)

steps.text: Kalimat-kalimat dari petisi latihan kepada dewan kota Bandung tentang Taman Melati, sebuah taman fiktif.

steps.title: Kontras dan pertanyaan
steps.text: Berikutnya: gaya bahasa yang bekerja lewat kontras, dan pertanyaan retoris.
steps.body:
**Antithesis** (antitesis): dua ide berlawanan dalam pasangan yang seimbang: *not X but Y* / *not X; Y*. *We are not asking for charity; we are asking for a fair chance.* Pembaca mengingat Y.
⚠ *Not only X but also Y* **menambah** Y dan tetap mempertahankan X, jadi bukan antitesis: *bukan … melainkan* ≠ *tidak hanya … tetapi juga*.
**Chiasmus** (kiasmus): kata-kata muncul lagi dengan urutan terbalik, A-B lalu B-A: *Good parks make good neighbours, and good neighbours make good parks.*
**Rhetorical question** (pertanyaan retoris): jawabannya sudah jelas, jadi pembaca menjawabnya dalam hati: *Do we really want our children's only playground to be a car park?* Satu pertanyaan menarik pembaca; deretan pertanyaan terdengar seolah kamu tidak punya bukti.

pairs.en: not only X but also Y
pairs.id: tidak hanya X tetapi juga Y (menambah)

steps.title: Sebutkan gaya bahasanya
steps.text: Sebuah op-ed di koran Surabaya mengkritik proyek bus yang tertunda.

question.prompt: Gaya bahasa mana yang dipakai penulis? 'We were promised cleaner buses. We were promised shorter journeys. We were promised a city that works.'
options: antithesis
chiasmus
anaphora
question.explanation: **We were promised** membuka ketiga kalimat: itu **anaphora** (anafora). (Ini juga tricolon, yang memuncak pada janji terbesar di akhir.) Tidak ada ide yang berlawanan, jadi bukan antitesis, dan tidak ada yang muncul lagi dengan urutan terbalik, jadi bukan kiasmus.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani, CEO sebuah perusahaan tekstil di Bandung, menulis surat kepada pemegang saham setelah membangun pabrik baru yang mahal.

question.prompt: Dia ingin kontras yang tajam. Kalimat mana yang memakai antitesis dengan benar?
options: Our new factory is not only a cost but also an investment.
Our new factory is not a cost; it is an investment in the next twenty years.
Our new factory is not a cost; it is not cheap either.
question.explanation: **Not a cost; an investment** mempertentangkan dua ide yang berlawanan, dan pembaca mengingat yang kedua. *Not only … but also* menambahkan investasi dan tetap mempertahankan biaya, jadi justru mengakui pabrik itu beban. Kalimat ketiga sama sekali tidak punya ide yang berlawanan.

steps.title: Membangun argumen yang persuasif
steps.text: Gaya bahasa itu hiasan; strukturlah yang meyakinkan. Ini rencana di balik teks yang kuat.
steps.body:
**Kenali pembacamu** (dewan kota peduli anggaran dan pemilih; pemegang saham peduli laba dan risiko) dan **bingkai masalahnya** dari sudut pandang mereka.
Pakai **tiga daya bujuk**: **ethos** (mengapa kamu layak dipercaya), **pathos** (apa yang harus mereka rasakan), **logos** (angka, sebab-akibat). Buat konkret: *212 trees*, bukan *many trees*.
Taruh **argumen terkuatmu di awal atau di akhir**, jangan terkubur di tengah.
Jawab keberatan sebelum pembaca mengajukannya (**prolepsis**): *Some will say a park is a luxury. In fact, …*
Tutup dengan **ajakan bertindak** (call to action): siapa, apa, kapan.
Kebiasaan orang Indonesia: pembuka seremonial yang panjang (*Dengan hormat, sehubungan dengan …*). Sampaikan masalah dan permintaanmu di beberapa kalimat pertama.

steps.title: Menulis untuk pembacamu
steps.text: Rina menulis surat kepada komisi anggaran dewan kota Bandung tentang Taman Melati. Para anggotanya paling peduli pada biaya.

question.prompt: Pembuka mana yang paling persuasif untuk pembaca ini?
options: Keeping Taman Melati costs the city about Rp 400 million a year; replacing the flood protection it gives us would cost an estimated Rp 6 billion.
Taman Melati is the heart of our neighbourhood, and every resident loves it dearly.
If the council destroys our park, Bandung will drown in floods and our children will suffer forever.
question.explanation: Pembuka pertama **membingkai masalah dari sudut pandang komisi** (uang) dengan angka yang konkret: logos untuk pembaca yang berpikir soal anggaran. Pembuka kedua adalah pathos yang tulus, tapi tidak menyentuh kepedulian mereka. Pembuka ketiga menakut-nakuti: ancaman yang dibesar-besarkan dan membuat penulis kehilangan kredibilitas.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina ingin menjawab kekhawatiran terbesar komisi itu sebelum mereka mengajukannya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Sebagian orang akan bilang kota ini tidak mampu membiayainya.
question.solution: Some will say the city cannot afford it.
question.explanation: **Some will say …** menyebutkan keberatannya dengan adil (prolepsis). Lalu Rina menjawabnya dengan bukti: *In fact, a single flood would cost far more.* Mengangkat keberatan itu sendiri menunjukkan rasa percaya diri dan membangun kepercayaan.

steps.title: Bujuk, jangan memanipulasi
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: di mana persuasi berakhir dan manipulasi dimulai.
steps.body:
Persuasi memberi alasan yang bagus; **manipulasi** memakai trik yang gagal saat diperiksa dengan teliti, dan pembaca yang menyadari satu trik berhenti memercayai sisanya.
**Fear-mongering** (menakut-nakuti): membesar-besarkan ancaman. *If the park goes, Bandung will drown.*
**False dilemma** (dilema palsu): hanya dua pilihan padahal ada lebih banyak. *Either we sell the land, or the city goes bankrupt.*
**Loaded question** (pertanyaan menjebak): pertanyaan yang menyembunyikan klaim yang belum terbukti. *Why is the mayor hiding the real cost?*
Emosi itu sendiri tidak salah: kisah nyata adalah pathos yang adil. Emosi menjadi manipulasi kalau dibesar-besarkan, dikarang atau dipakai sebagai pengganti bukti.

steps.title: Temukan triknya
steps.text: Ini kalimat-kalimat dari selebaran yang mendukung dan menolak sebuah mal baru di Bandung.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang merupakan dilema palsu (false dilemma)?
options: Some residents worry about traffic, and the developer has not yet published a traffic study.
Please come to the public hearing at the city hall on 20 May and give your view.
Either we build the mall, or Bandung's young people will have no future.
question.explanation: Kalimat itu hanya menawarkan dua pilihan, padahal ada banyak cara lain untuk menciptakan lapangan kerja bagi anak muda (proyek lain, pelatihan, usaha kecil): itu **dilema palsu**. Kalimat pertama adalah poin yang adil dan bisa dicek; kalimat kedua adalah ajakan bertindak yang jelas.

steps.title: Contekan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman, untuk op-ed, petisi atau surat kampanyemu berikutnya.

Kenali pembaca, bingkai masalah dari sudut pandang mereka, dan pakai angka yang konkret.
Emosi itu adil kalau benar dan didukung bukti; trik menghancurkan kepercayaan.
